newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains down on French falls, rain, sterling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains down on French falls, rain, sterling.

text.p: A weak French market, a strong sterling and rain sent LIFFE wheat lower.
November was the most active month, with 261 of total 851 lots traded. It last changed hands at 95.25 stg, 1.75 lower, but well off a low of 94.50 stg.
Barley also fell. Of a total 10 lots, six were on November, which last traded 1.75 stg down at 91.75 stg.

The market opened lower, taking its lead from a French market which had fallen after weekend rain. But sterling's rise made the downmove stronger. "It got sat on when the interest rate increased and the currency moved steadier," one trader said.

Sterling soared to above 2.83 marks in the aftermath of a rise in interest rates and the announcement of greater independence for the bank of England, although it gave up around one pfenning of the gain in late European trading.
But the fall on wheat started to look overdone at its lows and a combination of good support and sterling's partial recovery helped wheat to a late bounce, the trader said.
As in France, rain over the weekend, and on Monday, which was a holiday in the UK, was a bearish factor.

Southern England, including those grain producing areas worst affected by the drought, got some 7 to 12 millimetes of rain overnight, a spokesman for the London Weather Centre said. More is forecast for the rest of this week.
With no real physical export market, the focus is on the weather sensitive new crop, the trader said.
